title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Shared radix-4 combinational divider for RV32M
motivation:
The baseline achieves only 5.442 MHz; its reported worst path crosses
forwarding and the execute-stage ALU, taking 199.837 ns through 156 cells.
alu.sv expresses signed and unsigned division and remainder with separate
native / and % operators. These deeply combinational arithmetic networks
are the strongest suspected source of the long path. The experiment log
contains only the baseline, with no previous divider micro-optimizations.
Shortening this arithmetic circuit can increase fitness without adding
CoreMark cycles or changing how the pipeline handles either stalled bus.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU logic in alu.sv with a shared,
purely combinational unsigned radix-4 divider that produces quotient and
remainder together. Retain the existing ALU interface, multiplier, base
operations, and exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS substitutions.

For signed operations, form unsigned magnitudes of the two operands and
remember quotient sign = a[31] XOR b[31] and remainder sign = a[31]. For
unsigned operations, use the operands directly. Precompute zero-extended
D, 2D and 3D in 34 bits, with no truncation of 3D. Unroll 16 radix-4 digits
from the dividend's most significant pair to its least significant pair.
Starting with R=0, each digit forms T=(R<<2)|next_pair in 34 bits, computes
T-D, T-2D and T-3D concurrently using 35-bit unsigned subtractions, and
uses their borrow bits to select the largest valid digit 3, 2, 1 or 0.
Select the corresponding remainder and append that two-bit quotient
digit. Use subtraction borrow bits directly, avoiding a separate bank
of comparators followed by subtractors. The selected R fits in 32 bits
because R<D for every nonzero divisor. Feed the final magnitude quotient
or remainder through the appropriate conditional two's-complement sign
correction and select it by the ALU operation.

Handle divisor zero explicitly at the output: quotient is 0xffffffff,
remainder is the original dividend. Preserve DIV INT_MIN/-1 = INT_MIN
and REM INT_MIN/-1 = 0, either through the magnitude algorithm or exact
overrides. Do not use native / or % in the real synthesized divider.
This local arithmetic substitution reduces the number of serial digit
steps from 32 to 16, sharing all four RV32M division/remainder operations.
It adds no registers, busy handshake, stalls, or retirement changes.
The expected gain comes from Fmax at essentially unchanged CoreMark
cycles; concurrent subtractors and digit selection are the timing and
area tradeoff to check with the existing Gowin evaluation.

A fixed-width software model of this exact recurrence, borrow selection,
and sign correction matched quotient and remainder for 57,672 signed
and unsigned operand cases, including boundary values and deterministic
random pairs, and exercised all four quotient digits. FPGA timing and
RTL correctness still require the implementation-phase evaluation.

title: Move division out of the combinational execute path
motivation:
The only recorded bench experiment is the baseline: fitness 12.12,
median Fmax 5.442 MHz, and a 199.837 ns path through forwarding and
u_ex/u_alu with 156 cells. No LESSONS.md or earlier structural attempts
exist in this fixture. The ALU implements signed and unsigned division
and remainder with combinational / and % operators. These are likely
responsible for the very deep arithmetic path; even instructions that
do not divide must meet the clock constraint imposed by that hardware.
Moving this arithmetic behind registers should substantially improve
Fmax, at the cost of additional cycles only for DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the combinational divide/remainder cone with one shared,
blocking, registered divider in EX. Use unsigned restoring division
with four explicitly bounded quotient-bit steps per clock, eight
iteration clocks, operand magnitude capture at launch, and signed
correction on completion. Target at most ten EX clocks from accepting
a request to transferring its result under zero-wait memory, and at
most ten clocks between successive retirements for back-to-back divide
instructions. This keeps progress inside the existing formal liveness
window without changing any checker. Each iteration uses a 33-bit
partial remainder and subtract/borrow selection; do not infer / or %
or unroll all 32 quotient steps into a single combinational path.
Preserve single-cycle execution of every other ALU operation, including
the existing multipliers, to make this one divider-focused structural
change. A four-step iteration is a timing/latency compromise that cuts
the division depth by roughly eight while bounding the retirement gap.

Launch only for a valid, legal division instruction whose older MEM
instruction can advance. Capture both fully forwarded source operands,
the operation, and the instruction's RVFI source values exactly once.
Hold fetch and ID/EX while division is pending. Allow older EX/MEM and
MEM/WB instructions to drain: inject an invalid EX/MEM bubble with
side-effect controls cleared whenever the divider cannot transfer,
rather than repeatedly holding and reissuing the older memory operation.
Existing data-memory backpressure still holds an unaccepted memory
request and clears only MEM/WB valid as required for forwarding.
Hold a completed divider response until EX/MEM accepts it; consume it
exactly once, then resume normal EX/MEM forwarding to dependent users.
Gate redirects and architectural side effects by instruction validity
and actual stage advancement. Division must not create duplicate
stores, duplicate retirements, lost operands, or wrong-path requests.

Signed quotient correction uses dividend-sign XOR divisor-sign; signed
remainder uses the dividend sign. Preserve quotient all-ones and the
original dividend remainder for division by zero, and INT_MIN/-1's
defined quotient and zero remainder. Keep x0, illegal-instruction and
alignment traps, channel-0-only RVFI, and monotonic order unchanged.
Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS substitute only the documented arithmetic
formulas; retain the same request capture, iteration count, result
holding and pipeline handshake as real hardware, including for edge
operands. Keep every existing arithmetic vector and check through the
new clocked interface rather than deleting division coverage.

Validate divider results against an independent integer model with
truncation toward zero, then exercise pipeline dependencies and bus
stalls, run the unchanged formal suite, and require canonical CoreMark
CRCs and marker timing in cosim. Judge the change by the evaluator's
median Gowin Fmax multiplied by measured CoreMark iterations/cycle;
accept only if the clock gain exceeds the divide-cycle penalty and the
4.6 percent champion threshold. The main uncertainty is the remaining
multiplier or forwarding path becoming critical after division moves.

title: Small tagged next-PC predictor removes taken-control bubbles
motivation:
The baseline has no branch prediction: IF always selects PC+4, and EX
redirects and squashes the combinational IF/ID instruction on every taken
branch, JAL, or JALR. Because IF/ID is not registered, this wastes one
fetch opportunity per taken control transfer. CoreMark repeatedly executes
loops and calls, so learning their direction and target should recover
enough cycles to exceed the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold. The reported
Fmax bottleneck is the combinational arithmetic path; a small predictor
should improve iterations per cycle without lengthening that path. There
are no recorded predictor attempts or distilled lessons in this fixture.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 32-entry direct-mapped, fully tagged next-PC predictor inside IF.
Index with PC[6:2], tag with PC[31:7], and store an aligned target[31:2],
a conditional/unconditional bit, a two-bit saturating direction counter,
and valid. Read asynchronously in parallel with instruction fetch, without
adding a pipeline stage. On a valid tag hit, predict the cached target for
an unconditional transfer or a conditional branch whose counter MSB is 1;
otherwise predict PC+4. This predicts JAL/JALR as well as conditional
branches through the same table; do not add another predictor mechanism.
Keep the implementation small and reset only entry-valid bits, allowing
tag/target/counter storage to infer compact memory where supported. Read
the old entry on simultaneous lookup/training; no EX-to-IF table bypass
is necessary because the prediction actually used travels with the fetch.

Carry the selected predicted next PC in if_id_t and id_ex_t. When a fetch
is actually accepted into ID/EX, advance the PC to that prediction; hold
the PC and prediction payload appropriately during load-use and data-bus
stalls. Prediction itself must neither suppress the fetched instruction
nor flush ID. In EX compute the architecturally resolved next PC using
the existing forwarded operands and misalignment/trap behavior. Compare
it with the saved predicted next PC for EVERY valid instruction, including
ordinary instructions and illegal encodings. Issue a corrective redirect
and squash the younger fetch only when these next PCs differ. Correctly
predicted taken transfers therefore capture their target instruction
instead of inserting the baseline bubble. A wrong taken prediction must
recover to PC+4; a wrong target must recover to the resolved target.
RVFI pc_wdata must always report the resolved next PC, never a prediction.

Train exactly once when a valid EX instruction advances into EX/MEM, not
while EX/MEM is frozen, not for bubbles, and not from squashed instructions.
Conditional branches cache PC+imm even when not taken and update the
two-bit counter toward the actual outcome; initialize a new/replaced
entry weakly toward that outcome. Legal aligned JAL/JALR cache the resolved
target and are always predicted taken on a hit. Invalidate a matching entry
if its instruction now resolves as an ordinary instruction, an illegal
instruction, or a misaligned control transfer. Full tags make index
collisions misses; saved predictions make replacement and old-data reads
harmless. Do not train misaligned targets. Gate both training and recovery
with valid EX advance (!stall_ex_mem), so a held branch cannot repeatedly
move the fetch PC or repeatedly change its counter. On an advancing
misprediction, correction must override instruction-bus stalls and
load-use stalls; during data-bus freeze keep the entire younger pipeline
held and perform correction when EX can advance. Preserve all decoder,
arithmetic, memory side-effect, trap, and nret=1 retirement contracts.

Verify directed branch loops, both directions of misprediction, same-index
tag replacement, alternating JALR targets, stale-entry/non-control recovery,
and aligned/misaligned transfers. Exercise each with imem backpressure,
load-to-branch hazards, and an older blocked data-memory operation; verify
the exact retired PC/instruction sequence and absence of wrong-path stores.
Run the existing decoder/ALU/pipeline tests, single-channel formal checks,
and stalled CoreMark cosim with canonical CRC and timing-marker validation.
Evaluate median Gowin Fmax times measured iterations per cycle. The forecast
is an 8 percent fitness gain from fewer control-flow bubbles, with nearly
unchanged Fmax; poor table locality or routing overhead are the main risks.

title: Two parallel radix-4 digits per divider iteration
motivation:
The champion scores 85.94 at 38.602 MHz. Its reported worst path starts
in divider remainder state and passes through execute, taking 31.264 ns.
Each registered divider iteration still contains four serial restoring
bit steps with a wide subtraction and borrow-controlled remainder mux.
The earlier fully combinational radix-4 attempt gained only 3.38 percent
because it retained sixteen dependent digits and priority selection.

halve the serial digit count between registers and use flat selection.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the four serial radix-2 steps within each divider iteration
with two radix-4 digits. Each digit computes its three candidate
subtractions concurrently and selects the remainder with one-hot
masks and a balanced OR tree. Preserve request capture, exactly eight
iteration clocks, final-edge EX/MEM transfer and response holding.
This is a local divider datapath change; retain the existing pipeline,
bus-stall handling, forwarding, ALU interface and nret=1 RVFI contract.

At the existing request-accept edge capture dividend magnitude, divisor
magnitude D, and 3D. Calculate 3D as D+(D<<1) in 34 bits before capture;
2D is a shift of the captured D and needs no independent state. Avoid
truncating either multiple. Keep the existing captured operation/sign
controls and zero-divisor quotient-negation suppression.

For the first digit form the 34-bit trial value
T={remainder_q[31:0], quotient_q[31:30]}. Compute
{1'b0,T}-{1'b0,D}, {1'b0,T}-{1'b0,2D}, and
{1'b0,T}-{1'b0,3D} concurrently using 35-bit differences. Let ge1,
ge2 and ge3 be the complements of their respective high borrow bits.
The mutually exclusive selections are sel0=!ge1,
sel1=ge1 && !ge2, sel2=ge2 && !ge3, and sel3=ge3.
Select T or the matching difference using masked candidates and a
balanced OR tree, avoiding nested priority if/else or ternary muxes.
The quotient digit bits are {sel2|sel3, sel1|sel3}.

Feed the selected low 32 remainder bits into the second identical
digit calculation, consuming quotient_q[29:28]. Register its remainder
and {quotient_q[27:0], first_digit, second_digit}. Thus each iteration
still produces four quotient bits and eight iterations complete RV32M
division. For nonzero D, each selected remainder is below D and fits
in 32 bits; keep full 34/35-bit trial arithmetic before selecting it.
For D=0 all three candidates succeed, selecting digit 3 at each step;
the quotient becomes 0xffffffff and the remainder reconstructs the
dividend magnitude. Preserve signed truncation toward zero, signed
remainder following the dividend, and INT_MIN/-1's defined results.
Keep the original sign-correction and finish/response logic unchanged.
Place real arithmetic under the existing non-ALTOPS branch and retain
all four documented ALTOPS formulas with identical transaction timing.

An isolated RTL prototype changing only divider.sv passed all 30
existing real-arithmetic ALU tests, including randomized RV32M results,
exact eight-iteration timing, captured operands, held responses, reset
cancellation and direct final-edge transfer. The unchanged Gowin flow
with core_bench_si.sv and the timed stall generator measured placement
options 0/1/2 at 43.080/43.449/43.449 MHz: median 43.449 MHz versus the
champion's 38.602 MHz, a 12.56 percent clock gain. Option 0 used 3067
LUT4s and 677 FFs versus 2885 and 644. Its worst path shifted to the
existing register-read/branch-flush/decode cone, at 28.507 ns, rather
than the divider. No other RTL was changed in this prototype.

Expect approximately 12 percent fitness improvement from Fmax at
unchanged CoreMark iterations/cycle. Full formal, stalled CoreMark CRC
and UART validation, marker-cycle measurement, and implementation-phase
median timing remain required; this timing probe is not a completed
fitness evaluation. Additional routing or a different implementation
of the selection tree could reduce the gain. Require the unchanged
evaluator's score to exceed the champion by more than 4.6 percent.

title: Retimed radix-4 divider with registered completion

parallel digit selection inside bounded registered iterations addresses
that lesson and the champion's measured bottleneck together.

title: 64-entry next-PC prediction on the registered-divider champion
motivation:
The current champion already removes combinational division from the
timed execute path and reaches 38.602 MHz at fitness 85.94, but still
fetches PC+4 and discards one younger fetch on every taken control
transfer. The earlier predictor experiment hyp-20260930-003-r1s2
reduced stalled CoreMark cycles from 4,491,485 to 4,208,674 (6.3%) and
passed formal and cosim. Its fitness remained 12.81 because it was
built on the old combinational-divider baseline, not the champion.
This is evidence for a useful predictor rather than evidence that
prediction cannot help the current core. Recovering similar cycles
at the champion's clock would yield about 6.7% more fitness, exceeding
the 4.6% acceptance threshold if predictor overhead stays small.

registered divider, its eight iteration clocks, finish-edge transfer,
ALTOPS timing, and all other arithmetic. The sole architectural change

predictor's capacity is intended to reduce conflict misses without
introducing associative lookup, global-history logic, a return stack,
extra fetch registers, or a new arithmetic path.

Index the table with fetch PC[7:2], compare the full PC[31:8] tag, and
store aligned target[31:2], conditional/unconditional kind, a two-bit
saturating direction counter, and valid. Lookup is asynchronous and
parallel with imem, using the current registered fetch PC; do not
decode imem_data or add a target adder on this lookup path. A valid
matching unconditional entry predicts its cached target. A matching
conditional entry predicts its target when the counter MSB is set.
Every other case predicts PC+4. Keep tag/target arrays unreset and
reset only valid bits, with compact distributed-memory inference
where supported. No combinational EX-training-to-lookup bypass is
needed: the exact selected prediction accompanies the instruction.

Add predicted_next_pc to if_id_t and id_ex_t and latch it with every
instruction accepted into ID/EX. Hold it during load-use, data-bus,
and divider stalls; clear it with flushed/bubble payloads. IF advances
to this prediction only when the fetch is accepted. A prediction must
not flush or suppress its own instruction. Correctly predicted taken
branches and jumps let the target instruction enter ID/EX on the edge
that the control transfer advances into EX/MEM, eliminating the current
bubble in this core's combinational IF/ID topology.

EX derives actual_next_pc from the existing forwarded branch operands,
JAL/JALR target logic, and existing illegal/misalignment behavior. Use
the same resolved value for RVFI pc_wdata and prediction comparison.
Compare actual_next_pc against the instruction's saved prediction for
every valid instruction, including ordinary, illegal, and faulting
instructions. Redirect to actual_next_pc and squash younger work only
on mismatch and actual EX advance, gated by !stall_ex_mem, !div_hold,
and !reset. A wrong taken prediction recovers to PC+4; a wrong target
recovers to the resolved target. Faulting transfers retain the current
linear recovery and suppressed link write. Never report a prediction
as architectural pc_wdata or permit speculative memory side effects.

Train exactly once on that same valid EX-advance event. For a legal
aligned conditional branch, cache PC+imm even when not taken and move
a matching entry's counter toward the actual outcome with saturation.
Initialize a replacement to weakly taken (2) or weakly not taken (1)
according to the resolved outcome; distinguish a matching conditional
entry from an old entry of another kind. Legal aligned JAL/JALR cache
the resolved target and are unconditional. Invalidate a matching entry
when the instruction is now ordinary, illegal, or a faulting transfer;
do not evict an unrelated tag for a noncontrol instruction. Never
install a misaligned target. Full tags prevent index aliases from
predicting unrelated PCs, and saved predictions make simultaneous
lookup/training and table replacement safe without bypass logic.

recovery until EX advances. On an advancing mismatch, correction
overrides imem-not-ready and load-use PC holds, and flushes ID/EX.

prediction held while older stages drain; neither train nor redirect

recovery for any stale division prediction must coexist with the
existing saved-operand/result transfer. Keep all decoder defaults,
legality, memory alignment, nret=1 ports, and contiguous RVFI order.

mispredictions, same-index different-tag replacement, changed JALR
targets, stale entries whose instruction changes to noncontrol or
illegal, and misaligned branch/jump targets. Check the retired PC and
instruction stream and absence of wrong-path stores with imem stalls,

title: Remove branch squash from the decode payload path
motivation:
The champion scores 103.38 at 46.433 MHz. Its worst Gowin path takes
27.624 ns through forwarding, execute, fetch flushing, hazard control,
and back into an ID/EX source-value register. Division is already
registered; prior divider-only micro-optimizations moved the bottleneck
into this branch-to-decode feedback cone. if_stage currently replaces
every instruction bit with a NOP on redirect, and id_stage clears the
entire ID/EX payload on flush. Both put late branch resolution onto
wide decode and operand data paths. No logged micro_opt attempt has
addressed this cone.

flush or redirect. Preserve redirect priority over every fetch stall:
a redirect updates PC even if imemReady is low. Invalid instruction
bits may be arbitrary; they must never become a valid EX entry.

In id_stage, separate payload updates from validity updates. Reset

immediate, register addresses, decoded controls, and instruction)

invalid fetched instruction may create a redundant hazard indication

title: Separate redirect squash from instruction payload capture
motivation:
The champion scores 103.38 at median Gowin Fmax 46.433 MHz, with
4,491,485 measured CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts
at EX/MEM destination state and crosses forwarding, execute, fetch,
hazards, and decode before reaching an ID/EX operand register:
27.624 ns through 43 cells. The earlier radix-4 timing probe also
exposed this register-read/branch-flush/decode cone. Both prior
structural hypotheses addressed division successfully; the critical
path has now moved to control feeding back into the front-end data.

redirect, and ID flush zeroes its entire payload. Thus late branch
resolution selects register addresses, decode results and operand
data in the same clock. A register-boundary restructuring can remove
that feedback without adding a branch bubble or changing division.

title: 64-entry next-PC predictor with validity-only recovery
motivation:
The current hyp-20260930-002-r2s1 champion reaches fitness 103.38 at
46.433 MHz but still loses a fetch opportunity on every taken branch,
JAL, and JALR. The predictor attempts in log.jsonl passed formal and
cosim: the 32-entry design reduced CoreMark cycles by 6.3%, and the
64-entry design reduced them from 4,491,485 to 4,197,517, a 6.5%
reduction. Both were evaluated on earlier arithmetic designs. The
second achieved 92.05 fitness at 38.640 MHz, with its worst path in
the old divider; neither tested prediction on the current retimed
divider. At the current clock, the observed 64-entry cycle count
would imply approximately 110.62 fitness, already 7.0% above 103.38.
However, the champion's current critical path runs through forwarding,
EX, IF, the hazard unit, and ID. A predictor must avoid extending that
feedback path. In particular, recovery should invalidate younger
instructions without driving their instruction bits, decoder inputs,
register-file addresses, and entire decoded payload to zero.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 64-entry direct-mapped, fully tagged next-PC predictor to the
CURRENT hyp-20260930-002-r2s1 RTL, coupled to validity-only recovery.
This is a single next-PC prediction experiment. Preserve the current
registered divider, four-bit launch seed, seven iteration clocks,
registered completion magnitude/sign, response transfer, ALTOPS path,
multiplier, register file, pipeline depth, and nret=1 interface. Do not
resurrect either earlier predictor's older divider or change arithmetic.

Index the table with fetch PC[7:2] and tag with PC[31:8]. Each entry
contains valid, full tag, aligned target[31:2], conditional versus
unconditional kind, and a two-bit saturating direction counter. Read
asynchronously from the registered fetch PC in parallel with imem.
A valid full-tag hit predicts the stored target for an unconditional
entry or a conditional entry with counter MSB=1; otherwise predict
PC+4. There is no instruction decode or target addition on a table-hit
path, no associativity, no global history, no return stack, and no
training-to-lookup combinational bypass. Reset valid bits only; leave
tag, target, kind, and counter arrays unreset behind their valid gate
so Gowin can infer compact distributed memory. Old-data lookup on a
simultaneous write is safe because the exact prediction used travels
with the accepted instruction. Do not enlarge the table speculatively:
doubling 32 to 64 entries previously saved only another 11,157 cycles.

Add predicted_next_pc to if_id_t and id_ex_t. Capture it with every
accepted instruction, retain it with that instruction through stalls,
and advance fetch to it only when ID accepts the fetch. A correctly
predicted taken transfer admits its target instruction to ID/EX on
the same edge that the transfer advances into EX/MEM. Prediction does
not flush its own instruction. Retain the existing one-cycle repair
latency on a mismatch; do not add a fetch stage or recovery stage.

EX computes an architectural resolved_next_pc independently of the
predictor, using the existing forwarded operands, branch comparator,
jump targets, JALR low-bit clearing, and current trap behavior. Use
PC+4 for ordinary, illegal, and faulting transfers; use the resolved
target only for legal aligned taken branches and jumps. Use this same
resolved value for the existing RVFI pc_next payload and the saved-
prediction comparison. Compare for every valid advancing instruction,
including noncontrol instructions: a stale table hit must recover even
if the instruction changed to ALU, memory, division, or illegal code.
Redirect to resolved_next_pc only when it differs from the prediction
that accompanied that instruction. Prediction never determines RVFI
pc_wdata, trap, register results, or memory effects. Never truncate a
target or PC comparison to the CoreMark address range.

Factor mismatch detection to keep the branch decision off a serial
target-selection-then-32-bit-equality path. Compute equality of the
saved prediction against PC+4, PC+imm, and the resolved JALR target
in parallel, then select the appropriate one-bit equality using the
actual outcome and legality/alignment. The result must be exactly
equivalent to predicted_next_pc != resolved_next_pc for every encoding.
Architectural pc_next and corrective redirect_target still use the
actual resolved PC; this factoring changes only recovery logic timing.

Make the recovery datapath timing-conscious rather than retaining
the existing redirect-to-NOP-to-hazard-to-decode chain. IF/ID instruction
bits and register-file read addresses come directly from imem_data;
do not select NOP or zero instruction bits based on redirect or flush.
An advancing correction explicitly clears ID/EX.valid. In id_stage,
reset still initializes the complete register, but a flush only clears
valid; other fields may capture raw decoded data or retain their prior
value as appropriate for their hold enable. Payload capture/hold
decisions must not depend on redirect through masked instruction bits.
Concretely, give non-valid ID/EX fields a reset-or-!stall update rule
independent of flush, and give valid a reset/flush-first rule followed
by !stall capture. Do not implement flush-only invalidation by freezing
every data field on flush, which would retain recovery in their enables.
No semantic reliance on cleared bubble control fields is permitted:
branch/divider launch, hazard checks, forwarding producers, retirement,
and memory side effects must be qualified by the owning stage's valid.
The existing EX next_payload='0 for invalid input already isolates
downstream stages. Preserve the deliberate MEM/WB forwarding history
during dmem holds; do not indiscriminately gate that history by its
cleared retirement valid bit.

Compute load-use dependencies from raw fetch source fields, qualified
by fetch availability (imem_ready and !reset) and the valid EX load,
without feeding redirect back through the instruction or hazard match.
A match on a fetch being squashed is harmless: correction has priority
over the PC hold and ID/EX flush has priority over the ID hold. Keep
flush_if/flush_id bookkeeping consistent with these semantics; do not
feed recovery into raw decoder/operand data. Imem backpressure emits
an invalid younger instruction while allowing older work to advance.
During load-use bubbles hold PC, clear ID/EX.valid, and let the load
advance. During dmem backpressure hold PC, ID/EX and EX/MEM, and retain
the existing MEM/WB data with valid cleared. Gate recovery and training
with valid EX advance, !stall_ex_mem, !div_hold, and !reset. Correction
on an advancing instruction overrides imem-not-ready and load-use PC
holds. A blocked branch must correct and train once when it advances,
never repeatedly while its older memory operation remains blocked.

Train the same predictor exactly once on valid EX advance. For legal
aligned conditional branches, install PC+imm even when not taken and
saturate a matching conditional entry's counter toward the actual
outcome. Initialize a replacement weakly toward that outcome. For
legal aligned JAL/JALR, install the actual target as unconditional;
changing JALR targets must repair through the saved-prediction compare.
Invalidate a matching entry for a noncontrol, illegal, or faulting
instruction, without evicting an unrelated tag for noncontrol code.
Do not install misaligned targets, including a currently not-taken
branch's misaligned candidate target. Such branches can execute normally
without prediction; if taken, retain the existing trap and linear
recovery. Training uses existing branch/target results and must not
gate the ALU/divider result mux or response handshake. During division
retain the instruction's prediction in the held ID/EX register;
a stale division prediction repairs once on the response-transfer edge,
while the result and saved forwarded operands transfer unchanged.

Extend directed pipeline tests with warm taken loops, saturation and
both outcome mispredictions, full-tag collisions, changing JALR targets,
stale entries changed to ordinary/illegal/division instructions, reset
invalidation, and aligned/misaligned branch and jump targets. Check
the exact retired PC/instruction stream, actual RVFI next PC, contiguous
order, link values, and absence of wrong-path stores. Exercise imem
stalls, an older blocked load/store, load-to-branch dependencies, and
divider capture/completion/response backpressure. Include invalid
bubbles carrying nonzero decoded control fields, so validity-only
recovery cannot accidentally launch arithmetic or memory transactions.
Retain all existing tests and unchanged decoder legality/trap checks.
Run the existing pipeline/decoder/ALU suites, nret=1 formal gates, and
stalled CoreMark cosim with canonical CRCs, UART and marker validation.

Judge median Gowin Fmax times bracketed CoreMark iterations/cycle. The
forecast is a 10% fitness gain: approximately 7% from the previously
observed cycle reduction, with modest extra timing margin from removing
redirect-controlled instruction/payload masking on the current critical
path. This timing gain is a hypothesis, not a measured result. With
4,197,517 cycles, Fmax must exceed about 45.39 MHz to beat 103.38 by
4.6%; if clock stays 46.433 MHz, cycles must be below about 4.294 million.
Table routing, comparison/recovery fanout, and correctness of validity-
only bubbles are the main risks. Preserve the champion arithmetic and
evaluate vendor timing; an IPC gain alone is insufficient acceptance.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the three real combinational multiply expressions with ONE
shared signed 33x33 multiplication, using operation-dependent sign
extension on its inputs. Keep every multiplication at the existing
single-cycle EX latency. This is one local arithmetic-sharing micro-
optimization: retain the champion pipeline, predictor, divider,
forwarding, bus stalls, retirement width, and architectural results.

Define a_signed = (op == ALU_MULH || op == ALU_MULHSU) and
b_signed = (op == ALU_MULH). Form signed 33-bit operands
mul_a = $signed({a_signed && a[31], a}) and
mul_b = $signed({b_signed && b[31], b}). Compute an explicitly signed
66-bit product = mul_a * mul_b. MUL returns product[31:0]; MULH,
MULHU, and MULHSU all return product[63:32]. A zero leading bit
represents every unsigned 32-bit source as positive; the leading
operand sign bit represents signed sources exactly. The 66-bit
intermediate also represents unsigned products above 2^63 without
treating them as negative. Do not use 32-bit signed casts, discard
carry into bit 32, or apply serial post-multiply sign corrections.
MUL deliberately uses unsigned inputs since its low 32 bits are
identical for all signedness interpretations.

Put this single multiplication in the real arithmetic ifdef branch,
with no independently connected mul_ss, mul_uu, or mul_su expressions.
Keep the four exact documented RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas in their
existing branch. Preserve every nonmultiply ALU result and the entire
registered divider transaction, including its launch seed, seven
iterations, registered completion, and held-response handshake.
Use portable RTL so Gowin can infer its native large multiplier;
no vendor primitives, extra arithmetic stages, or clock changes.
Make all three high-half multiply cases select the same product
slice, so signedness selection is confined to two input extension
bits rather than three wide result networks. The intended benefit
is fewer DSP blocks, lower operand fanout, and simpler high-product
selection and routing on the measured critical path.

A scratch RTL prototype of exactly this shared expression passed all
30 existing real-arithmetic ALU cocotb tests, including randomized
multiplication and unchanged division transaction checks. Its Gowin
placement option 0 reached 49.115 MHz versus 46.008 MHz for the
champion on the same option, a 6.75 percent clock improvement, and
used two DSP blocks versus six. Logic changed from 3662 to 3671 and
registers stayed at 902. Its longest arrival was 25.654 ns, now a
forwarding-to-divider-launch path, with multiplication at 25.650 ns.
This is prototype timing evidence, not an accepted fitness result:
the evaluator's median placements and canonical CoreMark run still
determine acceptance. A four-half-product compressor implementation
was also probed but was slower at 43.173 MHz despite fewer DSPs;
use the shared full-width expression specified here, not that tree.

title: Registered shared multiplier removes multiplication from fast EX
motivation:
The champion scores 117.75 iter/sec at 49.426 MHz and 4,197,517
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst Gowin path takes 27.030 ns
through register-file/ID/EX/ALU/EX logic. Earlier structural attempts
successfully removed combinational division and separated its final
recurrence from sign correction. Validity-only recovery already
removed the branch-to-decode feedback path. The ALU still computes
three combinational 64-bit multiplication products from forwarded
operands, feeding the ordinary ALU-result mux. Registered, shared
multiplication is the remaining promising structural arithmetic
boundary: it can shorten the global clock period while charging
additional execution cycles only to the MUL family. The reported
module path does not identify the exact ALU operation, so multiplier
dominance is a hypothesis to verify with vendor timing.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move MUL, MULH, MULHU, and MULHSU out of the single-cycle ALU into
one blocking, registered unsigned 32x32-to-64 multiplier. Establish
three EX edges under ready buses: capture the fully forwarded
operands and operation; register their unsigned 64-bit product;
transfer the selected, signed-corrected result into EX/MEM. These
registers separate forwarding, multiplication, and result correction.
Use one shared inferred unsigned product, never three parallel
signed/unsigned multipliers. Keep ADD, shifts, comparisons, branches,
loads/stores, and the current divider on their existing schedules.
This is one multiplier-focused structural change; preserve the
current predictor and its validity-only recovery.

For U = unsigned(a) * unsigned(b), MUL returns U[31:0] and MULHU
returns U[63:32]. MULHSU returns U[63:32] - (a[31] ? b : 0), modulo
2^32. MULH returns U[63:32] - (a[31] ? b : 0) - (b[31] ? a : 0),
modulo 2^32. Register operands, operation, and the product before
these corrections. Use explicit operand/result widths and unsigned
arithmetic for the corrections. Do not leave any combinational
multiplication cone connected to the fast ALU-result selection.
Infer the DSP product with portable RTL and confirm mapping in the
unchanged Gowin flow. If the correction becomes critical, implement
its three-operand modular sum using carry-save reduction and one
final carry-propagate adder within the response-to-EX/MEM interval.
Do not add more execution cycles or change the division engine.

Reuse the proven divider transaction discipline for multiplication.
Launch once only for a valid legal MUL-family instruction when the
older EX/MEM instruction can advance. Capture the fully forwarded
rs1/rs2 values and RVFI metadata exactly once. Hold fetch and ID/EX
while this instruction is pending. Let older EX/MEM and MEM/WB work
drain; inject an invalid EX/MEM bubble whenever multiplication is
waiting and MEM can advance, rather than replaying an older store.
Preserve dmem backpressure holding the unaccepted older request and
MEM/WB payload history with valid cleared for stalled forwarding.
Hold the completed product, sources, operation, and metadata stable
until EX/MEM accepts the response; consume it once and release ID/EX
on that edge. Resume normal EX/MEM bypass to dependent consumers.
MUL and DIV share EX ownership, so their launches/responses cannot
overlap or overwrite each other's saved payload.

Keep EX redirect and predictor training tied to the valid instruction
actually advancing. A stale next-PC prediction on multiplication is
corrected once on response transfer, while its saved source values
and arithmetic result retire together. Invalid retained payloads and
wrong-path multiplication must never launch. Reset cancels pending
work. Preserve x0, decoder default-illegal and all legality checks,
alignment traps, single-channel nret=1 ports, in-order retirement,
contiguous rvfi_order, bus handshakes, and every correctness gate.

same operand capture, intermediate register, response holding, and
three-edge EX timing as the real multiplier. Keep the current DIV
ALTOPS and real paths unchanged. Retain all existing arithmetic
vectors and adapt tests to wait on the multiplier handshake. Add
signed/unsigned boundary and randomized independent integer-model
comparisons, response backpressure, reset cancellation, consecutive
MUL operations, ALU/load producers, dependent branch/store consumers,
and mixed MUL/DIV streams. Check forwarded RVFI operands, one store
service per accepted request, absence of wrong-path side effects,
exact retirement order, and bounded ready-bus progress.

title: Precompute predictor recovery candidates before execute

The champion already has a fully tagged 64-entry next-PC predictor,
parallel EX prediction comparisons, and validity-only recovery. Prior
doubling from 32 to 64 entries saved only 11,157 CoreMark cycles. A
sequential replay of the unchanged champion's retirement trace estimates

accuracy alone therefore has little headroom against the 4.6 percent
acceptance threshold. Instead, reduce the execution-stage cost of
verifying and recovering predictions by computing operand-independent
next-PC candidates and their prediction equalities before ID/EX.

gain over 117.75. The prototype has 3,584 logic cells and 966 registers,
versus 3,662 and 902 for the champion. Formal remains to be run by the
implementation/evaluation phase; prototype measurements are supporting
evidence and do not replace any correctness or fitness gate.

title: Two-entry predicted-path lookahead hides instruction stalls
motivation:
The champion already has a 64-entry next-PC predictor, but its fetch PC
is frozen whenever decode is held by load-use, data-memory backpressure,
or blocking MUL/DIV. Thus it cannot fetch predicted-path instructions
during those otherwise unused bus opportunities. About 22 percent of
instruction-bus cycles stall independently of those holds. A tiny elastic
queue can retain useful predicted-path fetches during holds and supply
them when the pipeline resumes despite a coincident instruction stall.
This targets iterations per cycle rather than marginal branch accuracy.
Prior predictor accuracy improvements have little remaining headroom;
isolated early-verification prototypes on this champion reduced Fmax.

motivation:

title: Resolve-trained return stack for multi-caller functions
motivation:
The champion's 64-entry next-PC table predicts every JALR with one last
resolved target per instruction PC. Returns from functions used at several
call sites therefore overwrite one another even when their BTB tags hit.
CoreMark repeatedly calls shared CRC and list helpers, making returns a
promising remaining source of avoidable corrections. Recent experiments
that retimed predictor maintenance or separated payload activation lost
Fmax; leave that machinery alone and improve the predicted target instead.

Classify legal aligned JAL/JALR instructions using the standard RISC-V
link-register hints: x1 and x5 are link registers. JAL pushes PC+4 when
rd is a link register. For JALR, a link rs1 with a non-link rd pops;
a link rd with a non-link rs1 pushes; two identical link registers push;
two different link registers pop then push. Neither link register means
no stack action. A JALR requiring a pop is a return-prediction candidate
only when its immediate is zero; other JALRs keep their cached target
prediction while performing the hinted stack action. Reserved encodings,
illegal or misaligned transfers, bubbles and squashed instructions never
change the stack. Send classification and the real PC+4 push value with
the existing once-per-advance EX training event; do not add an EX-to-fetch
data bypass or move any existing predictor training to a later stage.

Maintain a circular eight-word full-width stack with a next-write pointer
and a saturating depth in 0..8. A push stores PC+4 and advances the pointer;
when full it discards the oldest entry. A pop with nonzero depth decrements
pointer and depth; an empty pop does nothing. Pop-then-push replaces the
top when nonempty and acts as a push when empty. Reset pointer and depth,
leaving invalid stack words unreset. There is no speculative stack update,
checkpoint, rollback, or flush: only older architecturally advancing
control transfers train it. Accept consecutive events and update exactly
once despite dmem stalls and MUL/DIV holds. A correcting instruction's
own legal action is retained; its younger wrong-path work has no action.

stack top; an empty stack or other entry uses the original predictor.

Tag collision remains a miss, and no instruction-bus predecoder is added
to the fetch-address path. Save the exact selected next PC when each fetch

into an instruction already accepted. Resolved-only updates deliberately
tolerate stale stack tops for tightly adjacent calls/returns and fetch
lookahead. The existing EX comparison corrects those predictions normally.

title: Balanced LUT4 comparison trees for branches and SLT
motivation:
The champion scores 191.13 at 77.593 MHz. Recent worst paths repeatedly
start at ID/EX rs2 bit zero and traverse EX and fetch control. Removing
branch-only faults from bypass eligibility and separating EX producer
delivery both regressed, so those control-cone rewrites should not be
repeated. The six branch conditions currently use native full-width
signed/unsigned relational comparisons and equality; ALU SLT/SLTU also
duplicate full-width comparisons. A balanced, LUT4-sized lexicographic
comparison network directly attacks operand comparison delay and
simplifies signed/unsigned predicate sharing without changing pipeline
edges or recovery timing.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 191.13 at 77.593 MHz. Recent worst paths repeatedly
start at ID/EX rs2 bit zero and traverse EX and fetch control. Removing
branch-only faults from bypass eligibility and separating EX producer
delivery both regressed, so those control-cone rewrites should not be
repeated. The six branch conditions currently use native full-width
signed/unsigned relational comparisons and equality; ALU SLT/SLTU also
duplicate full-width comparisons. A balanced, LUT4-sized lexicographic
comparison network directly attacks operand comparison delay and
simplifies signed/unsigned predicate sharing without changing pipeline
edges or recovery timing.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace native full-width relational comparisons in the EX branch
comparator and ALU SLT/SLTU with the same balanced comparison topology.
Build one tree for the branch operands and one for the ALU operands;
share signed/unsigned predicates within each consumer, not a physical
comparator across different operands. Keep every architectural operand,
target adder, other ALU operation, bypass qualifier, predictor, pipeline
register and transaction schedule unchanged. This is one comparison-
logic micro-optimization.

Partition rs1 and rs2 into sixteen two-bit slices. For each slice j,
compute E[j]=(rs1[2*j+:2]==rs2[2*j+:2]) and
L[j]=(rs1[2*j+:2]<rs2[2*j+:2]) as unsigned two-bit comparisons.
Each leaf has four input bits and fits a LUT4. Combine adjacent ranges
with the MORE SIGNIFICANT range H and less significant range K:
E=E_H & E_K; L=L_H | (E_H & L_K). Build explicitly balanced levels
16 -> 8 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1; do not use a serial accumulator or a wide
subtractor to recover the final comparison. The final E is equality
and final L is unsigned less-than for all 32 bits. Derive signed
less-than as L XOR (rs1[31] XOR rs2[31]), which is exact for two's
complement operands and avoids a second full-width comparator.
Apply the identical recurrence to ALU a/b, returning {31'b0,L} for
SLTU and {31'b0,L XOR (a[31] XOR b[31])} for SLT. Leave ALU input
selection and every noncomparison integer and M operation untouched.

Use these shared predicates in the existing branch_op case: BEQ=E,
BNE=!E, BLT=signed_lt, BGE=!signed_lt, BLTU=L, BGEU=!L, default=0.
Preserve branch_taken's existing valid/legal/branch qualifications,
target alignment traps, link suppression, full-width predicted-PC
verification, immediate redirect and once-per-advance training. Do
not alter branch target arithmetic or use predicted outcomes for
architectural decisions. Keep complete registered source values,
EX-over-MEM-over-RF bypass priority, load-use handling, held memory
requests, MUL/DIV request/response timing, real and ALTOPS arithmetic,
reset behavior, validity-only squash, nret=1 IO and retirement order.

Validate the comparator against independent native integer equality,
unsigned comparison and signed two's-complement comparison. Exercise
every possible pair of two-bit leaf values, equal full operands,
each possible most-significant differing bit, opposite signs,
INT_MIN/INT_MAX, zero/all-ones, and deterministic random full-width
pairs. Check all six branch kinds, reserved branch-op defaults,
taken and not-taken alignment faults, unchanged prediction repair,
invalid/illegal instructions and stalls. Keep existing assertions
and run the unchanged pipeline suite, nret=1 formal, reference cosim
and canonical stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker validation.

An isolated two-file RTL prototype measured 80.242 MHz on Gowin
placement option 0 versus 76.000 MHz for an unmodified same-option
control, a 5.58 percent clock gain. LUT4 usage fell from 4925 to 4859;
FF, LUT RAM, BSRAM and DSP counts remained 1921, 24, 7 and 2. The
worst path moved to the unchanged divider, at 17.757 ns. The existing
real-arithmetic ALU suite passed all 36 tests. A software model of
the comparison recurrence matched independent signed/unsigned integer
comparisons and equality for 101,024 cases. The branch prototype
passed the three existing EX tests and 88,392 additional checks of
all eight branch_op encodings against independent integer outcomes.
A combinational SAT miter proved the tree's equality, unsigned
less-than and signed less-than equivalent to native comparisons
for arbitrary 32-bit operands, without assumptions.

The final two-file prototype measured 80.242/81.557/81.557 MHz on
Gowin placement options 0/1/2: median 81.557 MHz versus 77.593 MHz,
a 5.11 percent gain. The unchanged stalled CoreMark validator passed

title: Eight-entry predicted-path fetch reservoir hides instruction backpressure
motivation:

bracketed CoreMark cycles. Predictor history shows little remaining
benefit from direction accuracy or return targets: the return stack

title: Last-outcome direction prediction removes counter feedback
motivation:
The champion scores 200.89 iter/sec at median 81.557 MHz and
4,059,766 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Predictor history shows limited
accuracy headroom: a return stack saved only 2,196 cycles, banking
lost timing and an eight-entry reservoir saved only 30,671 cycles
while losing 11.52 percent fitness. The current two-bit counters
require a training-address read, matching-tag/kind selection and
saturating read-modify-write logic. Test a smaller direction policy
that removes this feedback while keeping the successful tagged
target table and two-entry lookahead intact.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace each two-bit saturating direction counter in the existing
64-entry tagged next-PC table with one last-outcome bit. This is one
direction-predictor simplification experiment. Keep the exact
PC[7:2] index, complete PC[31:8] tags, thirty-bit aligned targets,
valid bits, conditional kind, immediate training and recovery,
two-entry fall-through queue and every other RTL mechanism unchanged.

A valid full-tag unconditional hit still predicts its stored target.
A matching conditional row predicts its target exactly when its
last-outcome bit is one; otherwise predict PC+4. On every qualified
legal aligned control-flow installation write taken_q[train_index]
directly from train_taken, alongside the existing tag/target/kind
payload writes. There is no direction-counter read at train_index,
saturation arithmetic, matching-counter reuse test or direction
forwarding. Initial allocation, replacement and changed kind use
the same direct outcome write. Unconditional transfers write one.
Reset only validity; unreset direction data stays hidden on misses.

Retain the original full-tag train_match solely where needed for
noninstalling ordinary/illegal/uncacheable invalidation. Such an
instruction invalidates only its own currently matching full tag;
do not import allocate-only or snapshot-based invalidation from prior
experiments. Keep aligned-target installation, including rejection
of a not-taken branch's misaligned candidate, and old-data lookup
on simultaneous training. The only changed policy is conditional
direction learning. Use a portable one-bit array with one fetch
read address and the existing qualified synchronous write address.

Save every accepted fetch's exact full-width predicted next PC as
before, including both queue slots and empty fall-through. Later
direction updates must never change a queued or held prediction.
EX continues verifying every advancing instruction against its
independently resolved full-width architectural next PC, including
ordinary, illegal, misaligned and blocking M instructions. A wrong
direction is corrected through the existing immediate redirect and
validity-only younger squash before any wrong-path side effect.
Train once on the unchanged valid EX-advance event, never repeatedly
during bus/M holds or from a prefetched or squashed instruction.

Preserve queue capacity/acceptance and full simultaneous transfer,
redirect priority, load-use bubbles, complete decode operand bypass,
MUL/DIV capture/iteration/response ownership and real/ALTOPS arithmetic,
decoder default-illegal discipline, alignment traps, both memory
handshakes, resolved RVFI values, nret=1 IO, contiguous channel-0
retirement and forward progress. Do not change evaluation files,
formal bounds, benchmark sources or any invariant-enforcing check.

Update the independent predictor model to last-outcome learning.
Test all indices, full-tag replacement and upper-bit-only differences,
unchanged matching/nonmatching invalidation, conditional-to-unconditional
transitions, reset and lookup/update old-data semantics. Exercise
stable directions, alternating outcomes, isolated reversals, loop
exit followed by re-entry and a branch held through multiple bus
stalls. Assert that each actual advance writes its outcome exactly
once and that imem/decode holds alone cannot train. Retain exact
saved-prediction and FIFO checks, all architectural retirement and
wrong-path-store assertions, and existing trap/arithmetic coverage.

Run unchanged nret=1 formal including liveness, reference cosim,

Measure bracketed cycles and median Fmax across all three Gowin
placement options. Inspect synthesis to verify direction state and
its training-address read/modify/write cone actually shrink. The
risk is extra first-taken misses after loop exits; any clock gain
must exceed that cycle penalty. The unchanged divider may remain
limiting. Forecast six percent more fitness with low confidence
until measured. Acceptance requires fitness above 210.131 iter/sec;
